results.one_line: Res. SBS 01015-2026 makes the anti-money-laundering (SPLAFT) duties of Peru's slot rooms and casinos stricter (supplier due diligence, a 30-day staff induction, an internal audit report, a longer annual compliance-officer report, prize winners in the operations register), and no packaged software covers it, but the market is small (about 325 firms), the duty is an update of an existing one that consultants already serve, and fines top out near 8 UIT (S/ 44,000).
results.buyers: 714 slot rooms and 19 casinos (Focus Gaming News 2022, matching a July 2026 MINCETUR figure). These are run by about 325 licensed firms, per an undated MINCETUR presentation to Congress from about 2023 that returned 404, so the count is unverified. There are also about 91 online gaming licences (El Búho, July 2026, a secondary source) that already use international KYC tools.
results.price: No public prices found for SPLAFT consultants, outsourced compliance officers or software. Plausible price: S/ 150-400 a month per small operator, or S/ 800-1,500 a month for a consultant managing many firms (an estimate). Benchmarks: SME payroll software costs S/ 75-280 a month; outsourced bookkeeping costs about S/ 1,050 a month. The maximum fine is about S/ 44,000 (8 UIT at S/ 5,500).
results.top_competitor: Law firms and consultants selling SPLAFT setup and outsourced compliance officers (for example PRCP and Caro & Asociados), plus free SBS list checks and the ROSEL/SISDEL filing portals. For online operators, GBG and KYCAID are registered KYC providers.
results.killer: No hard killer. The main risk is that the market is too small and enforcement too weak: about 325 firms that already have compliance officers and manuals under Res. 1695-2016, and the only public SPLAFT sanctions found were 10 firms in 2022. The adaptation deadline could not be confirmed.

results.one_line: SEPRELAD Res 196/2020 gives about 1,640 registered vehicle traders a recurring AML workload (manual, compliance officer, KYC, quarterly negative reports, annual evaluation, external audit), and no vertical tool covers it. But the market is small and informal, enforcement is warnings and 60-day registry suspensions rather than fines, and I found no price evidence.
results.buyers: 1,642 vehicle importers, dealers and consignors on SEPRELAD's obliged-subject register (GAFILAT Mutual Evaluation 2022, Table 55). Older counts: 1,142 used-car lots in 2019 (Última Hora); CIVU has only about 110 members. Adjacent SEPRELAD sectors using the same template: real estate 1,658, jewellers 162.
results.price: No published prices for manuals, outsourced compliance or the SEPRELAD-registered external audit (unverified). Plausible pricing: USD 150-300 setup plus USD 15-30 a month, with an optional bundle with a partner auditor at USD 500-1,000 a year (estimate).
results.top_competitor: Law firms and SEPRELAD-registered external auditors doing bespoke manuals and audits (e.g. Ferrere, Amaral); Compliance Paraguay sells only a PEP database. SEPRELAD's free SIRO portal covers ROS and negative-report filing only.
results.killer: None found. The biggest risk is a small, largely informal market with weak monetary enforcement: no fines on non-financial firms through 2021, only 704 warnings and 329 60-day registry suspensions, and just 27 audits filed for 2021. Few firms may pay for a tool, and auditors or consultants may bundle manuals.

results.one_line: Funded Paraguayan non-profits face real recurring duties: the 30 June beneficial-owner update (Ley 6446), the annual forms A-E and a website fund-use page every six months (Ley 7363 / Decreto 4806/2025). But all filings go through the free MEF SIARA portal, the paying segment is small and hostile to the law, and the law faces pending constitutional challenges, so the best fit is a cheap transparency-page and calendar tool sold through accountants.
results.buyers: No official count found for SIARA, the beneficial-owner register or SEPRELAD (unverified). Estimate: a few hundred to about 2,000 professional NGOs and foundations that get public or donor funds; the 2025 budget sends over Gs. 56,000M to NGOs (abc.com.py, 16 Jan 2025). CEJ cites more than 10,000 comisiones vecinales (abc.com.py, 10 Jul 2024), but Decreto 4806/2025 art. 6 covers them only if they handle public funds.
results.price: Plausible price: Gs. 150,000-350,000 a month (about USD 20-45) per organisation, or a per-client rate for accountants (unverified). What they pay today: the SEPRELAD system fee of about Gs. 400,000 a year, plus accountant or law-firm fees, for which no public prices were found. Fines under Ley 6446 are 50-500 jornales (about Gs. 5.9M-58.5M), plus RUC blocking.
results.top_competitor: The free MEF SIARA portal (siara.mef.gov.py), which handles registration, beneficial-owner filings and forms A-E. Decreto 4806 art. 14 also lets organisations publish on the authority's portal in justified cases. Beyond that, law and accounting firms (Ferrere, Berkemeyer) advise on these duties; no Paraguayan SaaS was found.
results.killer: No single killer. The main risks together: the filing itself is free on SIARA; the paying market is small and short of money; two constitutional challenges seek to suspend Ley 7363 (Dec 2025 and Jul 2026); and no published fines on non-profits were found.

results.one_line: From 1 Jan 2027 every Kazakh kindergarten needs a preschool-education licence or it loses the state order. No kindergarten-specific readiness tool exists. But the job is mostly one-off, the real blockers are premises and land rather than paperwork, roll-out is phased over about 3 years, and Atameken is still lobbying for a transition period.
results.buyers: About 6,526 private kindergartens out of 11,909 preschool organisations, 96% of them with the state order (Education Ministry via Tengri, Apr 2026). About 3,070 mini-centres in 2023 (National Statistics Bureau via kapital.kz). Almaty alone has 896 private kindergartens.
results.price: No market price found. The state fee is 10 MRP (about 43,200 tenge), and school directors working without a licence were fined over 92,000 tenge. Losing the state order (about 27,000 tenge per child per month, unverified) is the real stake. Plausible prices: a self-check and document pack at 20-50k tenge one-off, a done-for-you review at 150-300k tenge, and an inspection-readiness subscription at 5-10k tenge a month (all estimates).
results.top_competitor: General education-licensing consultants such as Ybcase (no published price, nothing preschool-specific), plus the free elicense.kz/eGov filing and regional quality-department briefings. No kindergarten-specific product was found.
results.killer: No single killer. The biggest risk is that this is a one-off licence (term unconfirmed) whose hardest requirements (premises ownership or a 5-year lease, land use, fire rules) software cannot fix. Demand is also spread out by a phased 3-year roll-out and possibly softened by the transition period Atameken requested on 1 Oct 2026.

results.one_line: Act 73/2026 forces Slovak accountants, tax advisers, auditors and estate agencies to register in goAML by 30 Nov 2026 and to check beneficial owners from several sources for every client. Registration is free, 92% of surveyed agencies already have an AML programme, and the FSJ ran only about 10 inspections in 2025, so a low-priced Slovak "AML desk" is a modest side product, not a strong business.
results.buyers: No official total. Press says "thousands" of firms and sole traders (pravnenoviny.sk). 223 estate agencies answered the FSJ AML questionnaire, which was sent out through ZRKS and NARKS; most have 0-1 employees, and 93 of 220 brokered 0-10 deals in 2024-25 (FSJ TPU-RS and PKC2026 on minv.sk). Counts of bookkeeping-licence holders, tax advisers (SKDP register) and auditors (SKAU) were not found. My guess is 3,000-6,000 realistic buyers (unverified).
results.price: Today buyers pay a law firm once: about EUR 600+ for an AML programme pack (AKMV) and EUR 130 for a consultation. goAML registration is free. A tool could plausibly sell at EUR 9-29 a month, or EUR 99-249 a year (unverified).
results.top_competitor: Free FSJ tools and guidance (the goAML portal, the FSJ guidance on what an AML programme must contain, FSJ opinions for accountants and tax advisers). Paid alternatives: one-off law-firm packs (AKMV, from EUR 600) and FinStat AML for PEP and beneficial-owner screening (price unverified). No Slovak AML workflow app for small firms was found.
results.killer: No single killer. The biggest risk is weak enforcement, which leaves little willingness to pay. In 2025 the FSJ started 10 inspections in total and its fines came to EUR 142k across 6 decisions. 92% of agencies already claim to have a programme. Buyers are tiny, and the free FSJ tools cover registration.

results.one_line: The FINTRAC duty for lessors, factors and cheque cashers is real (in force since 1 Apr 2025) and penalties have risen sharply, but the government counts only 865 covered businesses and associations, dealer platforms and consultants already cover most of the work. The best opening is a cheap compliance-programme kit for small lessors and dealers that finance or lease in their own name.
results.buyers: 865 newly covered businesses (65 factors, 600 cheque cashers, 200 financing/leasing companies; 761 of them small), per the government's regulatory impact statement for SOR/2025-67/68 in Canada Gazette Part II, 26 Mar 2025. Car dealers that finance or lease in their own name could add more, but how many there are is unverified (Canada has 3,783 franchised dealerships per CADA 2024 and about 7,560 used-car dealers per IBISWorld).
results.price: About $900-1,400 a year (roughly $79-129 a month) looks plausible. The government estimates compliance costs about $2.8k a year per small factor, cheque casher or lessor, plus 48 hours a year to maintain the programme. Consultants (KPMG, MNP, Substance Law, Doane GT) quote only on request; a programme build or two-year review likely costs $5-20k (unverified). UCDA gives Ontario dealers a template, and FINTRAC report filing is free.
results.top_competitor: UCDA's AML policy template, programme guidance and KPMG training for dealers. Dealertrack AML (Equifax), Paays AML Check and AutoCorp cover KYC and screening only. No product runs the whole programme for small lessors or in-house-financing dealers.
results.killer: Market too small: 865 officially counted entities, 600 of them cheque cashers in a crowded MSB market. Upside depends on whether dealers that only arrange third-party financing are covered; UCDA reads them as likely outside, and FINTRAC has not published a position.

results.one_line: REPSE contractors must file ICSOE (IMSS, LSS art. 15-A) and SISUB (INFONAVIT, art. 29 Bis) three times a year, and IMSS now publicly lists inconsistent filings. A tool that builds both files from payroll/SUA data and checks them against each other has no dedicated competitor. But filing is infrequent, a free portal with a bulk template exists, and accountants already absorb the work, so it fits best as a multi-client tool for accounting firms.
results.buyers: No official count. Proxies: 34,302 REPSE firms had a non-positive IMSS opinion in Feb 2024 (IMSS/STPS bulletin via taxtodaymexico.com), 14,455 were warned in Jul 2025 (IMSS Boletín 396/2025), and about 71k were registered by 2021 (unverified). STPS cancelled more than 51k registrations in 2025 (Tiempo). Estimated 40k-80k active filers (unverified). The IMSS ICSOE public list, downloadable in Excel, could give an exact count.
results.price: No published prices found for consultancies, templates or platforms. Proposed: MXN 250-500/month per contractor, or MXN 1,500-4,000/month for accounting firms with 10-50 RFCs (unverified). Today buyers pay accountant time of about 12 hours per four-month period (Praxium), roughly MXN 10k a year (estimate). The ICSOE fine is MXN 58,655-234,620 at the 2026 UMA.
results.top_competitor: The free IMSS ICSOE portal with its bulk-upload template and the INFONAVIT SISUB module, plus the contractor's accountant or payroll bureau. Unconfirmed threat: payroll suites (CONTPAQi Nóminas, Aspel NOI) may export the layouts. Client-side REPSE platforms (Xternall, BDO, AXA SUBTOOL) serve the client firms that hire contractors, not the contractors who file.
results.killer: None found. Biggest risk: low frequency (3 filings a year) plus free state portals and accountants who already do the work. A dominant payroll suite (CONTPAQi/NOI) may already export ICSOE/SISUB files (unverified).

results.one_line: The § 49(4) PBefG order-book and return-duty rule for Mietwagen is enforced hard in 2026, with authorities analysing app data and courts upholding permit revocations, and no tool builds an audit-ready register. But the TSE half is already sold by hardware vendors, the buyer pool is a few thousand shrinking platform fleets, and many of them breach the duty on purpose.
results.buyers: About 23,800 taxi and Mietwagen businesses in total (Taxiverband Deutschland Geschäftsbericht 2025). The Mietwagen subset that needs the order book is an estimated 4,000-8,000 firms (unverified). Berlin alone had 436 Mietwagen firms with 2,335 cars in March 2025, down from 695 firms in December 2023 (Berlin Senate press release, 11 Apr 2025).
results.price: Plausible: EUR 10-20 per car per month for an order register with return checks, or EUR 300-1,500 for a one-off self-audit report (unverified). Today firms pay about EUR 500+ per car for TSE hardware (IHK Lippe-Detmold), platform fees of 20-29%, and tax advisers. Uber's supplier portal is free. The stakes are permit revocation (8 and 16 cars in 2026 cases), PBefG fines up to EUR 10,000 and TSE fines up to EUR 25,000.
results.top_competitor: Platform back-offices: Uber supplier portal and FREENOW Fleet Partner Dashboard (free, hold the order data, Uber monitors returns internally). On the TSE side: certified taximeter and Wegstreckenzähler vendors. Fleet tools such as Fahrly sync Uber and Bolt trips but show no order book or return-duty feature.
results.killer: No single killer. The main risk is weak buyer incentive: compliance costs empty return trips, not paperwork, so violators won't buy and compliant firms may manage with platform exports. Added to that are reform lobbying to loosen the return duty (2021 reform evaluation due 2026) and the VGH München view that app-forwarded orders aren't valid, which creates liability for any "compliance proof" claim.
